29. Frequently Asked Questions
Can I return clothes after 25 days?
Yes, if the item is within the 30-day clothing return window and meets the condition requirements.
Can I return electronics after 20 days?
Normally not under the standard electronics return policy because electronics have a 14-day return window. If
the product is defective, the warranty process may still apply.
How long does a COD refund take?
Nimbus Commerce normally initiates an approved COD refund within 3 business days after return inspection.
Bank posting may require an additional 2–5 business days.
Can I cancel an order after it has shipped?
A shipped order normally cannot be cancelled. The customer can use the applicable return process after delivery.
Can I exchange shoes for another size?
Yes, normally within 30 days, provided the shoes are in eligible condition and the requested size is available.
What if I received a damaged product?
Report transit damage promptly, normally within 48 hours, and provide requested evidence. The claims team
may approve replacement, refund, repair, or another remedy.
Can I return an opened beauty product?
Opened beauty and hygiene products are generally excluded for ordinary returns. Defects, contamination,
incorrect items, or fulfillment errors are handled separately.

Normally no. Points can generally cover up to 30% of eligible merchandise subtotal and cannot be used for
excluded fees.

The customer should stop repeatedly retrying, verify payment details, and try another supported payment
method. Risk controls may require additional review.

No. First determine the applicable SLA, current tracking status, carrier exception, and whether a delivery
investigation is required.

on the product, destination, and reason for return.

4. COD Refund Timelines
Cash on Delivery (COD) orders require a separate refund workflow because the original payment was collected
in cash or through a delivery-agent collection process rather than through an online payment authorization.
4.1 Standard COD Refund Timeline
For an approved COD return, Nimbus Commerce normally initiates the refund within3 business days after
return inspection is completed. The customer may choose an eligible bank transfer destination or Nimbus
Commerce store credit, subject to the options displayed for the order.
After Nimbus Commerce initiates a bank refund, the customer’s bank may require an additional2–5 business
days to reflect the amount. Nimbus Commerce’s support agent should distinguish between the internal
refund-initiation timestamp and the bank-posting timestamp.
4.2 COD Refund Exceptions
If the customer has not provided valid bank details, the refund remains pending until valid details are received.
A refund can also be paused if the order is under a fraud review, the returned item does not match the order, or
required return components are missing.
If a COD refund has been marked “processed” but has not appeared after the normal banking period, support
should first verify the transaction reference and destination details before escalating to the payments team.
4.3 COD Partial Refunds
For orders containing multiple products, an approved return of only some products produces a partial refund.
Discounts, bundle pricing, shipping fees, loyalty-point usage, and promotional credits may affect the refundable
amount.
Example: if a customer buys three items under a bundle discount and returns one item, the refund is not
necessarily the standalone list price. The refund engine recalculates the allocation of discounts according to the
order’s promotion rules.

5. Delivery SLAs
Delivery Service Level Agreements (SLAs) define expected delivery ranges after an order is confirmed and
released for fulfillment. An SLA is an operational target and does not mean that every parcel is guaranteed to
arrive at the exact end of the stated range.
5.1 Domestic Delivery SLA
Service Processing target Delivery target Typical total
Standard 0–2 business days 2–5 business days 2–7 business days
Express 0–1 business day 1–2 business days 1–3 business days
Priority metro Same/next business day 1 business day 1–2 business days
Large-item delivery 1–3 business days 3–7 business days 4–10 business days
Business days exclude weekends and configured public holidays. Weather events, carrier disruptions, customs
processing, remote-area restrictions, and customer-requested delivery changes can extend the operational timeline.
5.2 Delivery Status Definitions
Order confirmedmeans payment and order validation have succeeded.
Processing means the order is being prepared but has not necessarily been handed to the carrier.
Shipped/in transitmeans the parcel has entered the carrier network.
Out for deliverymeans the carrier has assigned the parcel to a delivery route.
Delivered means the carrier reports a successful delivery event.
Delivery exceptionmeans a carrier or operational issue is preventing normal progress.
5.3 Late Delivery
A customer should normally be treated as experiencing a late delivery when the current date exceeds the
applicable promised delivery range without an approved exception.
For standard domestic parcels, support should first inspect tracking data. If there has been no carrier scan for
48 hours while the parcel is in transit, the support agent may open a carrier investigation.
A delayed parcel should not automatically be declared lost. The lost-package workflow requires the applicable
investigation threshold to be reached.

Calendar day: Every day, including weekends and holidays.

Return request: A customer’s submitted request to return a product. It is not the same as an approved return.

Refund initiated: Nimbus Commerce has sent the refund instruction to the payment/refund system.

COD: Cash on Delivery.
SLA: Service Level Agreement or operational delivery target.
Reverse pickup: Collection of a return parcel from the customer’s address.
Final sale: Product status indicating that ordinary change-of-mind returns are unavailable, subject to defect
